a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal

claims.claim: The query shares the dapagliflozin ethoxybenzyl-chlorophenyl aglycone, and dapagliflozin was absorbed at least 75% from a 50 mg oral solution in healthy subjects, directly supporting a high absorption component for the scaffold.

Dapagliflozin has good Caco-2 permeability comparable to compounds with good human absorption and is only a weak P-gp substrate (efflux ratio 3.8), so efflux does not provide affirmative evidence of F < 20%.

L6 hepatic data show dapagliflozin is hardly metabolized and most stable in human hepatocytes, with CYP-mediated oxidative metabolism <10% of total metabolism and low oxidative intrinsic clearance (4 µL/min/mg); glucuronidation is the major clearance route but does not establish low oral bioavailability.

Transferable L1/L2 gold contexts report absolute or systemic F values of 32-100% (nabumetone 32%, sorafenib 50%, atenolol 50-63%, betaxolol 80-89%, safinamide 95%, ciprofibrate ~90%), all above the 20% threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule.
No matched oral-versus-IV AUC or IV comparator data are supplied for the query.
The query's modified bicyclic sugar differs from dapagliflozin; its UGT/CYP phenotype, intestinal stability, and first-pass extraction are not directly measured.
No query-specific formulation, solubility, or gut-wall efflux data are available.
L6 hepatic clearance values (UGT1A9 CLint 30 µL/min/mg, biliary CLint 10.2 µL/min/g liver) are for dapagliflozin and are not directly translated to the query's F.
content.decision_summary: High: favorable physicochemical prior, all transferable gold contexts above 20%, dapagliflozin analog evidence shows ≥75% absorption, good permeability with only weak P-gp efflux, and high human hepatocyte stability with minor CYP oxidative metabolism; L6 hepatic clearance records do not provide affirmative low-F evidence. Confidence moderate because no direct query F measurement and the bicyclic sugar modification is not directly tested.
